episodes.186760: On December 25th and the 26th, a South Pacific Convergence Zone (SPCZ) moved over the American Samoa Islands. WSO Pago Pago recorded 2.36 inches of rain on the 25th and 3.77 inches on the 26th.
episodes.187119: Rain and above normal temperatures in the southern Red River Valley lead to flood warnings being issued for three sites in southeastern North Dakota. The rain fell on frozen ground, and thus immediately entered the river system.
episodes.187614: A deep low pressure system brought heavy rainfall to northwest North Carolina, particularly along the crest of the Blue Ridge in Watauga County.  Sustained southeasterly winds added an orographic enhancement to rainfall amounts which fell across the headwaters of the Watauga River. While rainfall rates generally remained at a half inch or less across southern Watauga County through the event, the duration of rainfall locally approached 36 hours.  Rainfall totals across the headwaters of the Watauga River were observed as high as 6.5 inches, while amounts further downstream near Sugar Grove were up to 3.5 inches. The prolonged rainfall resulted in minor flooding of the Watauga River, with no damage reported.
episodes.187904: A strong area of low pressure and associated frontal system brought heavy rain to the mountains and foothills of North Carolina rom Christmas night into the 26th. A swath of 5 to 7 inches of rain fell along and close to the Blue Ridge escarpment in about 24 hours. This resulted in localized flooding across the foothills and in the southern mountains. This event followed one of the driest autumns on record across the area, so flooding was not as bad as it would have usually been with these rainfall amounts.
episodes.187948: A weak cold front drifted southward over the Florida Keys.  A couple waterspouts were observed in association with convective rain showers developing ahead of the front.

events.county: Hawk Channel From West End Of Seven Mile Bridge To Halfmoon Shoal Out To The Reef
events.narrative: A waterspout was observed by the Monroe County Fire Rescue Department about 3 miles offshore oceanside near mile marker 32 of the Overseas Highway.  The condensation funnel cloud extended about one-quarter the way down from cloud base.

events.county: Straits Of Florida From West End Of Seven Mile Bridge To South Of Halfmoon Shoal Out 20 Nm
events.narrative: A waterspout was observed via the WFO Key West rooftop camera approximately 16 miles south southeast of Boca Chica Key.  The condensation funnel cloud extended about one-third the way down from cloud base, and no spray ring was observed.

Public reported multiple roads were inundated by floodwater and closed across the south side of Hendersonville after 4 to 6 inches of rain fell in about 24 hours. Portions of South Main St were inundated, including at King St and at Spartanburg Highway due to Mud Creek overflowing its banks. Greenways and outbuildings along Mud Creek were also flooded, with high water conditions continuing into the early morning hours of the 27th. Airport Rd was also flooded and closed due to inundation from Bat Fork.

The Watauga River at Sugar Grove (SGWN7) crested at 7.11 feet at 1:00 pm EST on December 26th due to prolonged moderate to heavy rainfall. This is the 20th-highest crest in the history of this gage, and is the highest crest since June 2019. This crest (3,290 cfs) ranks less than a 2-year event per USGS StreamStats.  No damage was reported with this event.

Significant flooding occurred on Fagaima road due to flash flooding and poor storm water drainage. Water flowed onto residential properties in the region. An estimated 7.5 inches of rain fell in the area on the 25th and 26th. An estimated 2.5 inches of rain fell between 6:50 AM and 8:50 AM on the 26th.
The Fargo gage on the Red River of the North (FGON8) crested at 18.64 feet on December 31st at 9 am.

A stream gauge on Johns River exceeded its established flood stage after 5 to 7 inches of rain fell over the headwaters in about 24 hours. Portions of Johns River Rd were inundated as was Corpening Bridge Rd. Additionally, media reported Spainhour Rd was flooded by a tributary of Warrior Fork.
